inputs.userGoal: Use Azure Cosmos DB as the canonical gallery and review store, use Microsoft Foundry to review newly collected items for publication, and let the gallery chatbot answer from approved catalog data.
subGoals: Cost-optimized development: pay-as-you-go MAI inference and serverless Cosmos DB in one region.
Security-first automation: GitHub OIDC, disabled local authentication, and workload-specific least privilege.
Bounded data use: reviewer and chatbot code query only required Cosmos records and pass bounded context to Foundry; the model receives no database credentials.
insightsApplied: insight-002: use the S0 Foundry resource tier and a system-assigned account identity in addition to workload identities.
insight-003: create dedicated user-assigned identities rather than reuse identities from other workloads.
insight-004: retain public endpoints for GitHub-hosted runners while disabling local authentication and enforcing Entra RBAC.
insight-005: tag every resource for ownership and cost tracking.
insight-006: use gallery-scoped CAF-style names with deterministic unique suffixes.
insight-007: require TLS 1.2 or later wherever the resource exposes a configurable minimum.

overallReasoning.summary: Cosmos DB is the canonical source for gallery items, candidate review state, and pipeline audit data. The managed API serves live committed gallery records and passes bounded context to Foundry for chat; the browser and MAI model never receive Cosmos credentials. Publication remains a separate decision-hash and ETag-guarded identity.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Public endpoints are retained because GitHub-hosted runners and the public chatbot gateway cannot reach private endpoints; local authentication is disabled and OIDC or managed identity is mandatory. Single-region serverless Cosmos and Functions reduce development cost. The constant catalog partition is appropriate for the current small gallery but must be revisited before 20 GB or sustained high write volume. MAI-Thinking-1 is preview and lacks documented JSON-schema output, so strict local validation and benchmark gating are required. APIM and an Entra-protected Function add components but prevent browser credential exposure and use the authenticated Function for durable rate limits while centralizing request limits, context selection, and evidence attribution. Exact tags apply where supported. No Key Vault is needed because no application secret or function key is created.

plan.validation: Every dependency resolves within the dedicated resource group or Entra application boundary. Serverless database and all five containers omit throughput. Only the publication identity has canonical/public catalog create/replace permissions; reviewer and API identities cannot mutate catalog items. Migration is a rerunnable create-only stage: map each current static record to type=catalog-item, catalogPartition=gallery, publicationStatus=published; reject any non-equivalent 409; require source count = Cosmos count = API count and canonical SHA-256 parity before declaring Cosmos authoritative. Publication binds decisionHash, catalogSnapshotHash, policy/model receipt hashes, operationId, and expected ETag; matching create conflicts are accepted only after point-read hash equality and every 412 fails stale. Deploy API resources stopped, verify storage/Cosmos/Foundry RBAC plus Entra app-role propagation and authsettingsV2, then start the Function and test Table-backed Function limits through APIM. All live activation, online validation, what-if, environment changes, migration, and deployment remain outside this draft planning phase.
architecturePrinciples: Cosmos DB is the canonical catalog and review source
GitHub Pages queries the committed public projection through the managed API
Applications pass bounded Cosmos context to Foundry; models hold no database credentials
Review decisions and catalog publication remain separate authorization boundaries
Gallery and chatbot API routes share one committed public projection
Migration requires count and canonical hash parity before cutover
Fail closed on model or provenance ambiguity
